tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
# 04 — Dual-ViT retraining and model publishing

**State: trained, published, wired into the pipeline. Evaluation unfinished.**
Updated 2026-11-13: the `training/` recipe was **rewritten** upstream and now
runs as Hub tasks — see *Where things live*.

## Run `ATAIIR2604_NorthSea`
Retrained both stages on the ATAIR validations, because the old ViT was out of
domain on v5a + isolated crops.

| Set | crops | classes | test accuracy |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| binary | 12,470 | 2 | **98.18%** |
| multiclass | 6,599 | 7 | **98.28%** |

Per class (multiclass F1): pluteus 99.0 (n=387), Copepoda 98.8 (377),
Appendicularia 98.5 (163), gelatinous 94.1 (34), Cnidaria 84.8 (19),
Chaetognatha 90.9 (6), Ctenophora 80.0 (4).

**Read the tail with care** — single-digit support means the macro average
(92.3 F1) says little. Cnidaria's 73.7% recall is the one real signal; it needs
more validated examples.

## Decisions baked in
* Binary not-living side = `Unknowns + not-living + bubble + t001` (artifacts
  belong with non-organisms).
* `multiple species` **excluded** from the multiclass set — fused objects are a
  segmentation problem for an object detector, not a naming problem.
* Classes under 20 crops dropped (cannot split train/val/test).
* Fine-tuned from the previous ViTs (lr 5e-5), not from ImageNet.
* Dedup matters: EcoTaxa subsets are **copies**, so 12,612 validated rows
  collapse to 12,470 distinct crops; last project wins.

## Deployment result on ATAIR (v5a + isolation + new ViT)
645,090 objects, **36,178 living (5.61%)** vs 7,255 (1.12%) with the old ViT —
about 5x. Totals identical, so this is purely the classifier.

**This number is not yet trusted.** The 98.2% test accuracy comes from a split
of the *validated pool*, which is not a random sample of all objects. Project
**23210** (500 random living calls + 500 random not-living) was built to measure
real precision and recall — **still unvalidated**. `gelatinous` is the most
likely over-call (3,792 predicted from 229 training examples).

## Where things live
* Recipe: `training/build_trainset.py`, `training/train_vit.py`,
  `training/README.md`. Landed as `cc30f6e`, then **substantially rewritten**
  (`a0c5b8d`, `f9e8482`) — if you remember the original scripts, re-read them:
  * Crops now come from the segmenter's **`result.h5` via
    `vit_classify_hdf5.iter_crops`** — literally the inference function, so
    training crops cannot drift from what inference produces. Old projects
    still train from `deconv_crops*.zip`. EcoTaxa **export** zips are
    deliberately *not* a source: their PNGs carry a scale bar (topic 06).
  * `train_vit.py` **asserts at startup** that its preprocessing equals
    `vit_classify_hdf5.preprocess`, and exits if it has drifted.
  * `--isolate-crops` reproduces neighbour isolation from the HDF5 mask.
  * Runs as three Hub tasks: `pisco_ecotaxa_labels` -> `pisco_vit_trainset`
    -> `pisco_vit_train` (topic 09).
  * Crops still deliberately not committed — they are derived (118 MB).
* Weights on Hugging Face, **all public**:
  `Veit/ATAIIR2604_NorthSea_{binary,multiclass}` (v5a + isolated) and
  `Veit/M181_{binary,multiclass}` (231204 + non-isolated, the pipeline default).
* Select with `--dualvit-model ATAIIR2604_NorthSea`; local dirs win, otherwise
  it resolves `<owner>/<run>_{binary,multiclass}` from the Hub
  (`PISCO_DUALVIT_HF_NAMESPACE`). Prints `(local)` or `(Hugging Face)`.
  Still present in `process_pisco_profiles.py` after the rebase.
  The HDF5 route selects a model per stage instead, via `pisco_vit_classify`.

## Open
* **Validate 23210** and compute precision/recall/F1 with CIs. If precision is
  high the 5x is real recovery; if not, the model over-calls.
* Recall needs the not-living half; at 500 draws it yields a bound, not a tight
  estimate.

## New-chat prompt
> Read docs/handoff/04-dualvit-training.md. I validated project 23210. Pull the
> results and compute precision, recall and F1 per class with CIs.

# 09 — PIScO Hub integration, and what it changes for us

**State: landed on both repos' GitLab `main`.** `process_pisco_profiles` is
now **reconciled** (this session's work rebased on top, 2026-11-13).
`pisco_segmenter` local is still **9 commits behind** and was reviewed
read-only — nothing pulled or merged.

> **The old behaviour is pinned.** `pisco_segmenter` GitLab branch
> **`pre-hub-background`** -> `b805b9a` is the exact code every result in
> topics 01-07 was produced with: per-frame rolling-window background, before
> the per-block change below. Created 2026-11-13. It is a pointer at a commit
> already on `main`, so it adds nothing and can be deleted freely.
> Check it out to reproduce or continue any of this session's runs:
> `git checkout -b pre-hub-background --track gitlab/pre-hub-background`

Read this first: it reframes where the other topics' code lives. Everything in
topics 01-07 was done on the **old python route**; the Hub work adds a
**second, now-primary route** through the C++ segmenter's `result.h5`.

## The two routes

| | old python route | HDF5 / Hub route |
|---|---|---|
| driver | `process_pisco_profiles.py`, `orchestrate_gpus.py` | Hub tasks in `toolbox.json`, `run*.sh` |
| crops | `Crops/`, `Deconv_crops/` + per-profile TSV | inside **`result.h5`** |
| export | `utils.create_ecotaxa_zips`, `export_ecotaxa_zips.py` | **`export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py`** |
| classify | in-pipeline dual ViT | **`vit_classify_hdf5.py`** |
| scale bar | not wired, old non-reversible fn | **on by default**, reversible (topic 06) |

Both still exist; the old route is what produced every number in this session.

## What landed on `process_pisco_profiles` (31 commits, 2026-09-09 .. 10-21)

A **closed retraining loop**, each step a Hub task with a `run_*.sh` wrapper:

```
segmenter result.h5
  → pisco_vit_classify     (vit_classify_hdf5.py; fp16 on tensor-core GPUs,
                            loader workers; chainable so stage 2 only sees
                            stage 1's living calls)
  → pisco_ecotaxa_export   (export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py; PNGs straight into the
                            zip from a process pool, predictions carried in
                            the TSV, scale bar, object_esd, sample_ctd_cast,
                            object_frame_index, link back to raw data)
  → pisco_ecotaxa_import   (ecotaxa_import.py; creates or adds to a project,
                            single pass since predictions ride along)
  → pisco_ecotaxa_features (ecotaxa_write_features.py; ViT CLS embeddings into
                            EcoTaxa so "similar to" works — the tool used
                            heavily during the not-living re-screening, topic 03)
  →  … humans annotate …
  → pisco_ecotaxa_labels   (ecotaxa_fetch_labels.py)
  → pisco_vit_trainset     (training/build_trainset.py)
  → pisco_vit_train        (training/train_vit.py, run once per stage)
  → back to pisco_vit_classify
```

Supporting pieces: `scale_bar.py` (topic 06), `crops.py` (`tight_masked`),
`ecotaxa_taxonomy_map.{py,json}` translating ViT labels to EcoTaxa taxon ids
— including the ATAIIR2604 multiclass labels — `ecotaxa_mirror.py` to copy
projects between EcoTaxa instances, and `ecotaxa_grant_annotators.py`.

Two details worth carrying:
* **Objects land as Biota**, with numeric EcoTaxa taxon ids written from the
  taxonomy map. The deprecated-taxon remap of topic 03 is the same problem this
  map now solves properly.
* `.gitignore` now excludes the **local** credentials file; only
  `process_pisco_profiles.config.example.json` is versioned (see topic 08).

## What landed on `pisco_segmenter` (9 commits, not pulled)
`88c8015` headless GPU worker · `0b8b3be` describe pipeline as a Hub tool ·
`87cd167`+`87df281` write `result.h5` alongside PNG/CSV · `acab6ed` make the
circular FOV mask switchable · `9f5fe67` **estimate the background as the C++
segmenter does** · `d15dcea` merge · `4af9b4d` **correct the background per
block** · `8eff671` read frames from a profile dataset as well as a directory.

**All four of this session's segmenter commits survive intact** on that branch
(`99a0d88`, `c1e03cd`, `8480520` crop isolation, `b805b9a` hang fix) — verified
by ancestry and by grepping the merged files.

## Does it change our workflow? **Yes — materially.**

### Background estimation changed, and there is no switch
| | before (what every result in this session used) | after |
|---|---|---|
| scope | per-frame **rolling window**, frame excluded | **per block of 12**, one background shared by the block |
| estimator | `np.max(bg_imgs)` | **max over pairwise minima** |

`PISCO_BG_SIZE` overrides the block size (default **12**); the *estimator*
itself has no legacy path.

**Why it was done** is sound and worth knowing: 12 is the stack the LUCYD
background textures were built with, so this keeps the **deconvolution input in
distribution**. That is a real improvement to the deconvolution step.

**But it changes the cleaned frame**, therefore the deconvolved crop,
therefore the thresholded contours. So:
1. **Object counts and crop appearance will differ** from everything recorded
   in this session. Abundances are not comparable across the change.
2. It is a **fourth domain shift** stacked on deconvolution model, crop
   isolation and classifier. Both published ViTs (`Veit/M181_*`,
   `Veit/ATAIIR2604_NorthSea_*`) were trained on **old-background** crops.
3. The gain is real but **unmeasured for classification** — better LUCYD input
   does not automatically mean better crops for a classifier trained on the old
   look. Treat it the way the deconvolution comparison was treated: measure,
   do not assume.

### Smaller changes
* **Input**: `frames.py` reads a directory **or** a `profile_dataset.h5`.
  Directory input still works, so existing invocations are unaffected.
* **Output**: `result.h5` is written **alongside** the PNGs and CSVs, not
  instead of them. Note its mask is **the object's own contour**, unlike the
  PNG crops, which are cut with the **accumulated frame mask** — independent
  confirmation of the accumulation behaviour found during the isolation work
  (topic 02). The HDF5 route's `--isolate` reproduces isolation from that mask.
* **FOV mask** is now overridable (`mask_img_override`); the default is
  unchanged (on).
* New knobs: `PISCO_BG_SIZE` (12), `PISCO_DECONV_BATCH`, `PISCO_LOG_FILE`.
* `run_profile.py` + `toolbox.json` package the segmenter as a Hub tool — a
  second entry point beside `orchestrate_gpus.py`.

## Decisions this forces
1. **Pull the segmenter or stay pinned?** Pulling silently changes the output
   of every future run. If SO308 is to stay comparable with the Madagascar
   subset already processed, either finish SO308 on the current code or re-run
   the two completed profiles after pulling.
   The `pre-hub-background` branch above makes "stay pinned" an explicit,
   reproducible choice rather than an accident of not having pulled — but note
   the local checkout is still on **`main`**, so a casual `git pull` there
   would still jump it forward mid-campaign. Switch the checkout to the
   pinned branch (a no-op for the files, same commit) if that risk matters.
2. **If standardising on the block background**, both ViTs want retraining on
   matching crops — and that is also the moment to settle the deconvolution
   choice (topic 02) and switch crop isolation on, so one retrain absorbs all
   three shifts instead of three retrains. The Hub loop above now makes that a
   chain of tasks rather than hand-run scripts.
3. **GitHub mirror of the segmenter is behind** and has not received these
   commits (topic 08).

## New-chat prompt
> Read docs/handoff/09-hub-integration.md. The segmenter's background
> estimation changed to per-block max-of-pairwise-minima and the HDF5/Hub route
> is now primary. I want to <measure the background change's effect on
> crops/classification before pulling / pull and retrain the ViTs through the
> Hub task chain / keep SO308 pinned to the current code>.

#! /usr/bin/env bash
#
# Hub wrapper for export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py.
#
# The Hub renders an INI settings file and passes its path as the single
# argument. The exporter itself is an ordinary CLI tool, so this wrapper's
# only job is to translate INI keys into flags — keeping the script usable
# by hand and the Hub integration thin.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
CONFIG_FILE="${1:-}"

if [[ -z "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: no settings file given." >&2
    echo "Usage: $0 <settings.ini>" >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: settings file '$CONFIG_FILE' not found." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Read one key from the INI. Values may carry inline comments and whitespace.
# A missing key must yield an empty string, not fail: the Hub omits optional
# settings entirely, and under `set -e` a non-matching grep would otherwise
# abort the script before it printed anything.
cfg() {
    grep -i "^[[:space:]]*$1[[:space:]]*=" "$CONFIG_FILE" \
        | head -1 \
        | sed 's/^[^=]*=//' \
        | sed 's/[[:space:]]*#.*//' \
        | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//' \
        || true
}

SOURCE_PATH="$(cfg sourcePath)"
TARGET_PATH="$(cfg targetPath)"
PROFILE_NAME="$(cfg profileName)"
MAX_ZIP_SIZE="$(cfg maxZipSizeMb)"
MIN_SIZE="$(cfg minSize)"
GAUGE_PRESSURE="$(cfg gaugePressure)"
LINK_BASE="$(cfg linkBase)"
PREDICTIONS="$(cfg predictionsPath)"
TAXONOMY_MAP="$(cfg taxonomyMapPath)"
SCALE_BAR="$(cfg scaleBar)"
PIXEL_SIZE="$(cfg pixelSizeUm)"
ISOLATE="$(cfg isolateCrops)"
CTD_CAST="$(cfg ctdCast)"

if [[ -z "$SOURCE_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: sourcePath is required." >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [[ -z "$TARGET_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: targetPath is required." >&2
    exit 1
fi

ARGS=("$SOURCE_PATH" "-o" "$TARGET_PATH")
[[ -n "$PROFILE_NAME" ]] && ARGS+=("--profile-name" "$PROFILE_NAME")
[[ -n "$MAX_ZIP_SIZE" ]] && ARGS+=("--max-zip-size" "$MAX_ZIP_SIZE")
[[ -n "$MIN_SIZE" ]] && ARGS+=("--min-size" "$MIN_SIZE")
[[ -n "$LINK_BASE" ]] && ARGS+=("--link-base" "$LINK_BASE")
[[ -n "$PREDICTIONS" ]] && ARGS+=("--predictions" "$PREDICTIONS")
[[ -n "$TAXONOMY_MAP" ]] && ARGS+=("--taxonomy-map" "$TAXONOMY_MAP")
[[ -n "$PIXEL_SIZE" ]] && ARGS+=("--pixel-size" "$PIXEL_SIZE")
[[ -n "$CTD_CAST" ]] && ARGS+=("--ctd-cast" "$CTD_CAST")
# Crop isolation is on by default; only an explicit falsey value turns it off.
case "${ISOLATE,,}" in
    0|false|no|off) ARGS+=("--no-isolate-crops") ;;
esac
# The scale bar is on by default, so only an explicit falsey value turns it off.
case "${SCALE_BAR,,}" in
    0|false|no|off) ARGS+=("--no-scale-bar") ;;
esac
# The Hub renders booleans as 0/1; accept the usual spellings too.
case "${GAUGE_PRESSURE,,}" in
    1|true|yes|on) ARGS+=("--gauge-pressure") ;;
esac

# h5py, skimage and PIL live in the torch venv on the workers. The Hub server
# runs its own (nix) Python; leaking it in produces confusing import failures.
unset PYTHONPATH PYTHONHOME
PYTHON="${PISCO_PYTHON:-/opt/pisco/venvs/torch/bin/python}"
if [[ ! -x "$PYTHON" ]]; then
    PYTHON="$(command -v python3)"
fi

echo "=== EcoTaxa export ==="
echo "Interpreter: $PYTHON"
echo "Source:      $SOURCE_PATH"
echo "Target:      $TARGET_PATH"
echo ""

exec "$PYTHON" "$SCRIPT_DIR/export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py" "${ARGS[@]}"

    echo "Error: settings file '${CONFIG_FILE:-<none>}' not found." >&2

fi

        | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//' || true
}

SOURCE_PATH="$(cfg sourcePath)"
TARGET_PATH="$(cfg targetPath)"
MODEL_PATH="$(cfg modelPath)"
ISOLATE="$(cfg isolateCrops)"
EMIT="$(cfg emitEmbeddings)"
BATCH="$(cfg batchSize)"
TOPK="$(cfg topK)"
WORKERS="$(cfg workers)"
PRECISION="$(cfg precision)"
RESTRICT_TO="$(cfg restrictToPath)"
RESTRICT_LABELS="$(cfg restrictLabels)"
CARRY_FORWARD="$(cfg carryForward)"

for required in SOURCE_PATH TARGET_PATH MODEL_PATH; do
    if [[ -z "${!required}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: $required is required." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done

ARGS=("$SOURCE_PATH" "-o" "$TARGET_PATH" "--model" "$MODEL_PATH")
[[ -n "$BATCH" ]] && ARGS+=("--batch-size" "$BATCH")
[[ -n "$TOPK" ]] && ARGS+=("--top-k" "$TOPK")
[[ -n "$WORKERS" ]] && ARGS+=("--workers" "$WORKERS")
[[ -n "$PRECISION" ]] && ARGS+=("--precision" "$PRECISION")
[[ -n "$RESTRICT_TO" ]] && ARGS+=("--restrict-to" "$RESTRICT_TO")
[[ -n "$RESTRICT_LABELS" ]] && ARGS+=("--restrict-labels" "$RESTRICT_LABELS")
# isolation is on by default; only an explicit falsey value turns it off.
case "${ISOLATE,,}" in 0|false|no|off) ARGS+=("--no-isolate-crops") ;; esac
case "${EMIT,,}" in 1|true|yes|on) ARGS+=("--emit-embeddings") ;; esac
# carry-forward is on by default; only an explicit falsey value turns it off.
case "${CARRY_FORWARD,,}" in 0|false|no|off) ARGS+=("--no-carry-forward") ;; esac

# torch and transformers live in the venv built from the official wheel; the
# Hub server's own (nix) Python must not leak in.
unset PYTHONPATH PYTHONHOME
PYTHON="${PISCO_PYTHON:-/opt/pisco/venvs/torch/bin/python}"
if [[ ! -x "$PYTHON" ]]; then
    echo "Warning: $PYTHON is not executable, falling back to the system python." >&2
    PYTHON="$(command -v python3)"
fi
# Fail on a clear message rather than a traceback from inside the script:
# a silently wrong interpreter is the confusing failure mode here.
if ! "$PYTHON" -c "import torch, transformers, h5py" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Error: $PYTHON cannot import torch, transformers, h5py. Set PISCO_PYTHON to an interpreter that can." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Models pulled from Hugging Face need a writable cache; /tmp is per-container.
export HF_HOME="${HF_HOME:-/tmp/hf}"

echo "=== ViT classification ==="
echo "Interpreter: $PYTHON"
echo "Model:       $MODEL_PATH"
echo ""

exec "$PYTHON" "$SCRIPT_DIR/vit_classify_hdf5.py" "${ARGS[@]}"

        | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//' || true
}

ARCHIVE="$(cfg archivePath)"
TARGET="$(cfg targetPath)"
PROJECT_ID="$(cfg projectId)"
PROJECT_TITLE="$(cfg projectTitle)"
INSTRUMENT="$(cfg instrument)"
VISIBLE="$(cfg visible)"
ACCESS="$(cfg access)"
UPDATE_MODE="$(cfg updateMode)"

URL="$(cfg url)"

for required in ARCHIVE TARGET; do
    if [[ -z "${!required}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: $required is required." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done

ARGS=("$ARCHIVE" "-o" "$TARGET")
[[ -n "$PROJECT_ID" ]] && ARGS+=("--project-id" "$PROJECT_ID")
[[ -n "$PROJECT_TITLE" ]] && ARGS+=("--project-title" "$PROJECT_TITLE")
[[ -n "$INSTRUMENT" ]] && ARGS+=("--instrument" "$INSTRUMENT")
[[ -n "$UPDATE_MODE" ]] && ARGS+=("--update-mode" "$UPDATE_MODE")
[[ -n "$URL" ]] && ARGS+=("--url" "$URL")
[[ -n "$ACCESS" ]] && ARGS+=("--access" "${ACCESS,,}")
case "${SKIP_EXISTING,,}" in 1|true|yes|on) ARGS+=("--skip-existing-objects") ;; esac
# visible defaults to true; only an explicit falsey value turns it off.
case "${VISIBLE,,}" in 0|false|no|off) ARGS+=("--no-visible") ;; esac

unset PYTHONPATH PYTHONHOME
PYTHON="${PISCO_ECOTAXA_PYTHON:-/opt/pisco/venvs/ecotaxa/bin/python}"
if [[ ! -x "$PYTHON" ]]; then
    echo "Warning: $PYTHON is not executable, falling back to the system python." >&2
    PYTHON="$(command -v python3)"
fi

echo "=== EcoTaxa import ==="
echo "Interpreter: $PYTHON"
echo "Archive:     $ARCHIVE"
echo ""

exec "$PYTHON" "$SCRIPT_DIR/ecotaxa_import.py" "${ARGS[@]}"

#! /usr/bin/env bash
#
# Hub wrapper for ecotaxa_write_features.py. Runs on the EcoTaxa machine,
# where the database is reachable on loopback.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
CONFIG_FILE="${1:-}"

if [[ -z "$CONFIG_FILE" || ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: settings file '${CONFIG_FILE:-<none>}' not found." >&2
    exit 1
fi

cfg() {

        | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//' || true
}

EMBEDDINGS="$(cfg embeddingsPath)"
PROJECT_ID="$(cfg projectId)"
PROJECT_ID_FROM="$(cfg projectIdFrom)"
PCA_PATH="$(cfg pcaPath)"
DSN="$(cfg dsn)"
ALLOW_PARTIAL="$(cfg allowPartial)"

for required in EMBEDDINGS PCA_PATH; do
    if [[ -z "${!required}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: $required is required." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Chaining hands over the producing task's directory, not the file in it.
if [[ -d "$EMBEDDINGS" ]]; then
    EMBEDDINGS="${EMBEDDINGS%/}/embeddings.npz"
fi

if [[ -z "$PROJECT_ID" && -z "$PROJECT_ID_FROM" ]]; then
    echo "Error: projectId or projectIdFrom is required." >&2
    exit 1
fi

ARGS=("$EMBEDDINGS" "--pca" "$PCA_PATH")
[[ -n "$PROJECT_ID" ]] && ARGS+=("--project-id" "$PROJECT_ID")
[[ -n "$PROJECT_ID_FROM" ]] && ARGS+=("--project-id-from" "$PROJECT_ID_FROM")
[[ -n "$DSN" ]] && ARGS+=("--dsn" "$DSN")
case "${ALLOW_PARTIAL,,}" in 1|true|yes|on) ARGS+=("--allow-partial") ;; esac

unset PYTHONPATH PYTHONHOME
PYTHON="${PISCO_ECOTAXA_PYTHON:-/opt/pisco/venvs/ecotaxa/bin/python}"
if [[ ! -x "$PYTHON" ]]; then
    echo "Warning: $PYTHON is not executable, falling back to the system python." >&2
    PYTHON="$(command -v python3)"
fi
# Fail on a clear message rather than a traceback from inside the script:
# a silently wrong interpreter is the confusing failure mode here.
if ! "$PYTHON" -c "import numpy, psycopg" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Error: $PYTHON cannot import numpy, psycopg. Set PISCO_ECOTAXA_PYTHON to an interpreter that can." >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== EcoTaxa feature write ==="
echo "Interpreter: $PYTHON"
echo "Embeddings:  $EMBEDDINGS"
echo "Project:     ${PROJECT_ID:-from $PROJECT_ID_FROM}"
echo ""

exec "$PYTHON" -u "$SCRIPT_DIR/ecotaxa_write_features.py" "${ARGS[@]}"

#! /usr/bin/env bash
#
# Hub wrapper for ecotaxa_import.py. Runs on the EcoTaxa machine, where the
# instance is reachable on loopback and the credentials file lives.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
CONFIG_FILE="${1:-}"

if [[ -z "$CONFIG_FILE" || ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: settings file '${CONFIG_FILE:-<none>}' not found." >&2
    exit 1
fi

cfg() {
    grep -i "^[[:space:]]*$1[[:space:]]*=" "$CONFIG_FILE" \
        | head -1 | sed 's/^[^=]*=//' | sed 's/[[:space:]]*#.*//' \
        | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//' || true
}

ARCHIVE="$(cfg archivePath)"
TARGET="$(cfg targetPath)"
PROJECT_ID="$(cfg projectId)"
PROJECT_TITLE="$(cfg projectTitle)"
INSTRUMENT="$(cfg instrument)"
VISIBLE="$(cfg visible)"
ACCESS="$(cfg access)"
UPDATE_MODE="$(cfg updateMode)"
SKIP_EXISTING="$(cfg skipExistingObjects)"
URL="$(cfg url)"

for required in ARCHIVE TARGET; do
    if [[ -z "${!required}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: $required is required." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done

ARGS=("$ARCHIVE" "-o" "$TARGET")
[[ -n "$PROJECT_ID" ]] && ARGS+=("--project-id" "$PROJECT_ID")
[[ -n "$PROJECT_TITLE" ]] && ARGS+=("--project-title" "$PROJECT_TITLE")
[[ -n "$INSTRUMENT" ]] && ARGS+=("--instrument" "$INSTRUMENT")
[[ -n "$UPDATE_MODE" ]] && ARGS+=("--update-mode" "$UPDATE_MODE")
[[ -n "$URL" ]] && ARGS+=("--url" "$URL")
[[ -n "$ACCESS" ]] && ARGS+=("--access" "${ACCESS,,}")
case "${SKIP_EXISTING,,}" in 1|true|yes|on) ARGS+=("--skip-existing-objects") ;; esac
# visible defaults to true; only an explicit falsey value turns it off.
case "${VISIBLE,,}" in 0|false|no|off) ARGS+=("--no-visible") ;; esac

unset PYTHONPATH PYTHONHOME
PYTHON="${PISCO_ECOTAXA_PYTHON:-/opt/pisco/venvs/ecotaxa/bin/python}"
if [[ ! -x "$PYTHON" ]]; then
    echo "Warning: $PYTHON is not executable, falling back to the system python." >&2
    PYTHON="$(command -v python3)"
fi

echo "=== EcoTaxa import ==="
echo "Interpreter: $PYTHON"
echo "Archive:     $ARCHIVE"
echo ""

exec "$PYTHON" "$SCRIPT_DIR/ecotaxa_import.py" "${ARGS[@]}"

#! /usr/bin/env bash
#
# Hub wrapper for ecotaxa_write_features.py. Runs on the EcoTaxa machine,
# where the database is reachable on loopback.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
CONFIG_FILE="${1:-}"

if [[ -z "$CONFIG_FILE" || ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: settings file '${CONFIG_FILE:-<none>}' not found." >&2
    exit 1
fi

cfg() {
    grep -i "^[[:space:]]*$1[[:space:]]*=" "$CONFIG_FILE" \
        | head -1 | sed 's/^[^=]*=//' | sed 's/[[:space:]]*#.*//' \
        | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//' || true
}

EMBEDDINGS="$(cfg embeddingsPath)"
PROJECT_ID="$(cfg projectId)"
PROJECT_ID_FROM="$(cfg projectIdFrom)"
PCA_PATH="$(cfg pcaPath)"
DSN="$(cfg dsn)"
ALLOW_PARTIAL="$(cfg allowPartial)"

for required in EMBEDDINGS PCA_PATH; do
    if [[ -z "${!required}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: $required is required." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Chaining hands over the producing task's directory, not the file in it.
if [[ -d "$EMBEDDINGS" ]]; then
    EMBEDDINGS="${EMBEDDINGS%/}/embeddings.npz"
fi

if [[ -z "$PROJECT_ID" && -z "$PROJECT_ID_FROM" ]]; then
    echo "Error: projectId or projectIdFrom is required." >&2
    exit 1
fi

ARGS=("$EMBEDDINGS" "--pca" "$PCA_PATH")
[[ -n "$PROJECT_ID" ]] && ARGS+=("--project-id" "$PROJECT_ID")
[[ -n "$PROJECT_ID_FROM" ]] && ARGS+=("--project-id-from" "$PROJECT_ID_FROM")
[[ -n "$DSN" ]] && ARGS+=("--dsn" "$DSN")
case "${ALLOW_PARTIAL,,}" in 1|true|yes|on) ARGS+=("--allow-partial") ;; esac

unset PYTHONPATH PYTHONHOME
PYTHON="${PISCO_ECOTAXA_PYTHON:-/opt/pisco/venvs/ecotaxa/bin/python}"
if [[ ! -x "$PYTHON" ]]; then
    echo "Warning: $PYTHON is not executable, falling back to the system python." >&2
    PYTHON="$(command -v python3)"
fi
# Fail on a clear message rather than a traceback from inside the script:
# a silently wrong interpreter is the confusing failure mode here.
if ! "$PYTHON" -c "import numpy, psycopg" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Error: $PYTHON cannot import numpy, psycopg. Set PISCO_ECOTAXA_PYTHON to an interpreter that can." >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== EcoTaxa feature write ==="
echo "Interpreter: $PYTHON"
echo "Embeddings:  $EMBEDDINGS"
echo "Project:     ${PROJECT_ID:-from $PROJECT_ID_FROM}"
echo ""

exec "$PYTHON" -u "$SCRIPT_DIR/ecotaxa_write_features.py" "${ARGS[@]}"

"""Run a ViT over the crops in the C++ segmenter's result.h5.

One stage of the dual-ViT setup. Chain two of these -- a binary
living/not-living pass over everything, then a taxon pass restricted to the
living ones -- rather than baking the two-stage structure into one tool:

    vit_classify_hdf5.py results/ -o stage1/ --model .../binary/best_model \\
        --emit-embeddings
    vit_classify_hdf5.py results/ -o stage2/ --model .../living/best_model \\
        --restrict-to stage1/predictions.csv --restrict-labels living

Crops are read from ``result.h5`` rather than from exported PNGs. That skips
the scale-bar strip and the pad/unpad round trip entirely, and keeps neighbour
isolation a choice made at inference time rather than a property baked into
files on disk.

**Preprocessing mirrors ``utils.custom_image_processor`` exactly** -- longest
edge to 224 via ``torchvision.transforms.functional.resize``, centre-pad to
224x224 with white, normalise to [-1, 1]. A classifier is only valid for crops
that look like its training data, so this must not drift; see
``training/README.md`` for what a mismatch has cost before.

classification head sees -- for every crop the stage looked at. Those feed

entirely for a project where any object lacks a feature vector.

matplotlib, umap and datasets at module scope, none of which are installed on

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Export EcoTaxa import archives from the C++ segmenter's HDF5 results.

The old Python pipeline writes per-frame CSVs plus crop PNGs on disk, which
``process_pisco_profiles.py`` turns into an EcoTaxa archive. The C++ segmenter
route produces neither: object crops, their masks and their bounding boxes all
live inside ``result.h5``. This script is the missing half — it reads that file
and emits exactly the same archive shape the EcoTaxa importer already accepts,
so ``upload_to_ecotaxa.py`` works on the result unchanged.

Input is ``result.h5``, written by ``Mode::OBJECT_EXTRACTION``:

    /                      @imageHeight @imageWidth @sourcePath
    /<frame name>/         one group per source frame
        boundingBoxX/Y/W/H (N,) int32   position and size in the full frame
        offsets            (N,) int32   start of each crop in the flat arrays
        cropPixelData      (M,) uint8   all crops concatenated, row-major
        maskPixelData      (M,) uint8   segmentation masks, same layout

Crop *i* is ``cropPixelData[offsets[i] : offsets[i] + W*H].reshape(H, W)``.

Two things make this better than exporting from the old pipeline's PNGs:

* If ``pisco_deconvolve`` ran before extraction, the crops in ``result.h5`` are
  already deconvolved — deconvolution rewrites the correction checkpoints in
  place and extraction reads those.
* ``maskPixelData`` is the segmenter's own mask, so morphometrics are computed
  from what the segmenter actually detected. The old pipeline had to re-derive a
  mask by re-thresholding the saved crop and keeping the largest contour.

Crops carry a reversible scale bar (``scale_bar.py``): the strip is appended
below the image and the original size recorded in the PNG, so the crop can be
restored byte-for-byte before it is used as classifier input.

Crops are inverted on the way out: the segmenter stores objects bright on a
dark ground, while EcoTaxa and the old pipeline's crops are dark on light. The
inversion happens before morphometrics too, so intensity features match the
other route.

Deliberately free of pandas and of ``utils.py`` (which imports torch and
transformers at module scope): an export job should not drag a GPU stack in.
The few shared constants below are duplicated for that reason.

With ``--link-base`` every object also gets an ``object_link`` pointing back at
the Hub, which resolves it to the HDF profile viewer opened on that object in
..... ARGS .....

content.content:
# 02 — LUCYD deconvolution models + crop isolation

**State: evaluated, decision pending.** Four models compared on identical
frames; crop isolation implemented. No model is "approved" yet because the
comparison is confounded by the classifier.

## Model comparison (3 ATAIR profiles, identical pipeline, only deconv changed)

| Model | Total objects | Living | Rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| v4 (`..._v4_20260722`) | 1,077,477 | 3,126 | 0.29% |
| v5d (`..._v5d_20260807`) | 1,076,221 | 4,526 | 0.42% |
| v5 (`..._v5_20260806`) | 799,922 | 6,812 | 0.85% |
| **v5a (`..._v5a_20260807`)** | **645,090** | **7,364** | **1.14%** |

Two trends as the model improves: **total detections fall** (fewer spurious
particles) while **living rises**, monotonically on every profile.

## The confound — read before choosing a model
The ViT was trained on crops from the **old 231204** deconvolution. A
controlled same-object test (`ctrl_deconv_vs_vit.py`) showed the newer models
push real plankton into not-living: 18 objects flipped living -> not-living,
0 the other way. So **a higher living rate here partly measures similarity to
the old model, not image quality.** Choosing a deconvolution on this metric is
circular; use human judgement on crop quality plus clip-independent
segmentation metrics instead.

Related: deconv crops are **hard white-clipped at 245**, so any benchmark run
on raw model output measures a different image from what the classifier sees.

## Crop isolation (`PISCO_ISOLATE_CROPS=1`, commit `8480520`)
Whites out every contour except the target, so a crop carries only its own

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Import an exported archive into EcoTaxa, creating the project if needed.

Creates a new project by default and imports into it; pass ``--project-id`` to
add to one that already exists. Several archives (a split export) go into the
same project, in order.

Nothing is copied. The Hub's shared storage is mounted inside EcoTaxa as a
subdirectory of its server load area, so an archive sitting in a workflow's
output directory is already visible to the importer -- this only has to
translate the path (``/mnt/pisco/x`` -> ``/pisco/x``).

The project id is written to ``import.json`` in the output directory, so a
following task can attach features to the project this one just created
without a human carrying the number across.

Credentials come from a file on the EcoTaxa machine rather than from task
settings, which are rendered onto shared storage in plain text.

Usage:
    ecotaxa_import.py /mnt/pisco/.../export -o out/ --project-title "M202 028-02"
    ecotaxa_import.py /mnt/pisco/.../x.zip  -o out/ --project-id 8
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_CREDENTIALS = "/opt/pisco/etc/ecotaxa.json"

# Where the Hub's shared storage appears inside EcoTaxa. The importer resolves
# source_path against its server load area, and the share is mounted there.
DEFAULT_SHARED_ROOT = "/mnt/pisco"
DEFAULT_LOAD_AREA_PREFIX = "/pisco"

# EcoTaxa's project access levels. "open" lets every logged-in user annotate
# and manage through the API, but the GUI ignores it and shows the project as
# view-only; for annotation by everyone use ecotaxa_grant_annotators.py.
ACCESS_LEVELS = {"private": "0", "public": "1", "open": "2"}

# Job states: Finished, Error, Asking (a question the import needs answered).
TERMINAL_STATES = {"F", "E", "A"}


def api(base, path, data=None, token=None, timeout=600, method=None):
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        base.rstrip("/") + "/api" + path,
        method=method or ("POST" if data is not None else "GET"),
        data=json.dumps(data).encode() if data is not None else None)
    request.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    if token:
        request.add_header("Authorization", "Bearer " + token)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
            body = response.read().decode()
            return json.loads(body) if body else None
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {path} returned HTTP {exc.code}: "
                         f"{exc.read().decode()[:500]}")

content.text:
No runs started. Here's what I found and what a run would look like.

## Dual ViT: yes, trained and published

Run `ATAIIR2604_NorthSea`, from the ATAIR validations ([04-dualvit-training.md](docs/handoff/04-dualvit-training.md)):

| stage | crops | classes | test acc |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| binary | 12,470 | 2 | 98.18% |
| multiclass | 6,599 | 7 | 98.28% |

Weights exist both locally and on the Hub:
- `/home/veit/PIScO_dev/ViT_ATAIIR2604_NorthSea_binary/best_model`
- `/home/veit/PIScO_dev/ViT_ATAIIR2604_NorthSea_multiclass/best_model`
- `Veit/ATAIIR2604_NorthSea_{binary,multiclass}` on HF (public)

Caveat that still stands: its ATAIR deployment gave 36,178 living (5.61%) vs 7,255 (1.12%) with the old ViT, and **that 5× is not yet trusted** — project 23210 (500+500 random draws, built to measure real precision/recall) is still unvalidated.

## What the new workflow would run for 20260423-1705

Input: `/mnt/filer/202604_ATAIR-BSH/202604_ATAIR-BSB_PISCO/20260423/20260423-1705` — 1,231 TIFFs, 7.6 GB.

| # | tool | what it does | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pisco_segment` mode `BACKGROUND_CORRECTION_AND_COMPRESSION` | C++ MPI, cleans + compresses frames | HDF5 correction checkpoints |
| 2 | `pisco_deconvolve` | LUCYD, rewrites crops **in place** in those checkpoints | — |
| 3 | `pisco_segment` mode `OBJECT_EXTRACTION` | thresholds the deconvolved frames | **`result.h5`** |
| 4 | `pisco_vit_classify` (binary) | `ATAIIR2604_NorthSea_binary`, `--emit-embeddings`, `--isolate-crops` | `predictions.csv`, `embeddings.npz` |
| 5 | `pisco_vit_classify` (multiclass) | `--restrict-to stage1/predictions.csv --restrict-labels living` | `predictions.csv` |
| 6 | `pisco_ecotaxa_export` | PNGs + TSV straight into a zip, scale bar at 22.5 µm/px, taxonomy map | `ecotaxa_*.zip` |
| 7 | upload | see blocker 5 below | EcoTaxa project |

Where: steps 1–3 would go to `/media/veit/T710_data/` (1.5 TB free), **not** `/mnt/pisco` — that share is only 94 G with 72 G free and lives on an NFS box at 192.168.178.28.

## Seven things to settle first

1. **None of steps 4–7 are registered in the Hub.** Its tool table has only `pisco_segment`, `pisco_deconvolve` and demo tools; `process_pisco_profiles` is not a `tool_provider`. Also, the Hub has never run a real profile — every workflow in `instance/app.db` is an August 2026 test or demo. So either I register the provider, or I drive steps 4–7 by hand (the `run_*.sh` wrappers and the Python scripts are plain CLI tools, so this works).

2. **The wrappers' interpreter doesn't exist here.** They want `/opt/pisco/venvs/torch/bin/python`; `/opt/pisco/venvs` is absent. Needs `PISCO_PYTHON=/home/veit/miniconda3/envs/pisco/bin/python` — I verified that env has ROCm torch 2.6.0 with the GPUs visible.

3. **Deconvolution model mismatch — the biggest one.** `pisco_deconvolve` hardcodes `MODEL_NAME = 'lucyd-edof-plankton_231204.pth'` ([deconvolution_model.py:15](../pisco_deconvolution_py/Deconvolution/deconvolution_model.py#L15)). The ATAIIR2604 ViT was trained on **v5a** crops. Per topic 02 the mismatch is directional and measured (18 objects flipped living→not-living, 0 back), so this needs `PISCO_SEGMENTER_MODEL_PATH=/home/veit/PIScO_dev/underwater-lucyd/models/lucyd-edof-plankton_v5a_20260807.pth`.

4. **The segmenter itself is different code.** Every ATAIR number came from the *Python* segmenter; this route uses the *C++* one with its own background correction (`imageStackSize=20, threshold=10, minContourArea=10, boundingBoxPadding=10`). And `result.h5`'s mask is the object's **own contour**, while the old PNG crops were cut with the **accumulated frame mask**. So object counts won't be comparable to 645,090 / 36,178, and the crops the ViT sees differ from what it was trained on (23022 is an old project — its training crops came from the python route's `deconv_crops*.zip`). This is a real domain shift, not a formality. Your local python segmenter is at `b805b9a` = the pinned `pre-hub-background` commit, so nothing has moved under you.

5. **EcoTaxa upload won't work as the chain assumes.** `ecotaxa_import.py` copies nothing — it needs a co-located EcoTaxa with the Hub share mounted in its load area. Nothing is listening on 8088 and `/opt/pisco/etc/ecotaxa.json` doesn't exist. The ATAIR projects are on `ecotaxa.obs-vlfr.fr`, so step 7 has to go through the old `upload_to_ecotaxa.py` (FTP/tus), or we stop at the zip.

6. **ENTE3 isn't anywhere.** Not in the repo, not in the cruise metadata (`folders_ATAIR.txt` lists bare timestamps). I need to know where it should land: `--profile-name` (which drives `sample_id` and the filenames), the EcoTaxa project title, or both.

7. Inodes are not a risk here — crops stay inside `result.h5` and the exporter writes PNGs straight into the zip.

## Two questions before I start

- **Deconvolution**: run with v5a to stay in the ViT's domain, or with the tool's default 231204? I'd use v5a.
- **How far**: stop at `result.h5` + prediction CSVs (fast, answers "does the new route work and what does it count"), or go all the way to a zip and an EcoTaxa project? The upload needs the obs-vlfr route decided.

Where should ENTE3 appear?

content.content:
# Getting started

Install the Hub, run it, register the example toolbox, and watch a
two-step chain go through. Twenty minutes on a laptop. Deploying on the
cluster with real workers is a different document:
[cluster-runbook.md](cluster-runbook.md).

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer (the cluster runs 3.13, the nix shell 3.12).
- `ssh` on the PATH, if you ever want to add a remote worker.
- Nothing else: the database is SQLite, the front end is server-rendered.

## Install

Two ways. Pick one.

**Plain virtualenv** — what the deployments use:

```bash
git clone git@git.geomar.de:team-optics/plankton/PIScO_Hub.git
cd PIScO_Hub
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/pip install -e .            # the `hub` CLI, into the same venv
```

`requirements.txt` carries the server's dependencies; `pip install -e .`
adds the CLI as a console script (`.venv/bin/hub`). The CLI needs only
`requests`, so on a machine that will *only* talk to a Hub you can install
it alone: `pip install /path/to/PIScO_Hub`.

**Nix dev shell** — a Python with every dependency, plus two helper
commands:

```bash
nix develop
run_server      # = python3 -u main.py from the repo root
hub …           # = python3 -m hub_cli
```

## Configure

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/setup_env.py
```

writes `.env` next to `main.py` with a random `FLASK_SECRET_KEY` and
`DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///app.db` (the file lands in `instance/`). The
server refuses to start without the secret. Both files are git-ignored.

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/create_user.py
```

asks for a username and password — the web login. Passwords are stored
as scrypt hashes; there is no self-registration.

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/create_api_token.py <username> cli full
```

prints a bearer token **once**; only its hash is stored. The last argument
is the scope: `read`, `operate` or `full` ([AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#authentication)
explains what each may do). Keep it for the CLI:

```bash
export PISCO_HUB_TOKEN=<the token>
export PISCO_HUB_URL=http://localhost:5000        # the default; set it for a remote Hub
```

content.content:
### 1. Put the frames where every machine can see them

```
/mnt/pisco/incoming/<your profile>/     # raw .png frames
```

### 1b. Or build the profile dataset first

The chain below reads a directory of named PNGs. During a cruise the frames
come from the camera without metadata; `pisco_prepare_profile` (toolbox
`pisco_profile_dataset`) turns the camera output plus the sensor log into
`profile_dataset.h5`, and both segmenters accept its directory as
`sourcePath` — `{"$from": {"task": 0, "output": "dataset"}}` in the next
step. Its parameters are the ones the `profile` template asks for.

### 2. Write the workflow

**The complete chain is the Hub's `profile` template** — defined in
[`examples/profile_template.json`](../examples/profile_template.json) and
installed with `scripts/install_template.py` (the Hub's database is not the
source of truth; the file is). It asks for the profile's facts — cruise,
station, instrument, position, the frame directory, the sensor log — and the
two ViT models, and runs nine steps: `pisco_prepare_profile` builds
`profile_dataset.h5` from the camera output and the sensor log, then segment,
deconvolve, extract, both ViT stages, EcoTaxa export, import and features.
Every setting is written out even where it is the tool's default, so the file
says what a run means. The settings are the ones settled in
`docs/pipeline-comparison-spec.md`: a 12-frame background block on both
routes, 30 px of padding around each object so the deconvolution model sees
enough of the frame, a texture-filled atlas, and crops handed to EcoTaxa and
the classifier as the object alone in a tight box (`isolateCrops`).

Hub is updated and running on the MSM147 code.

## Done

- **Backed up** the Hub DB → `/media/veit/T710_data/hub_backups/app.db.pre-msm147-update_20261113`
- **Stashed** your uncommitted `docs/cluster-runbook.md` edit — `git stash pop` on branch `toolbox-framework` to get it back. That branch still holds your local-only commit `509c175`; nothing was lost.
- **Fast-forwarded** `main` 121 commits to `gitlab/main` = `517949a` (*tools/profile_rename…*, today 14:10). It contains all of `toolbox-framework`, which stopped on 2026-10-20 mid-cruise — so `main` is the right MSM147 line.
- **Rebuilt the nix dev shell** (the flake gained `hdf5plugin`, `pyserial`, `pytest`; dropped `flask-sock`) and verified the imports.
- **Restarted the Hub**: old PID 1115376 (running since Aug 11) stopped, now PID 1263900 on port 5000, HTTP 302 to login. Migrations applied cleanly — 13 columns added (`workflow.params/template_id/template_name`, `machine.dedicated`, `task.cancelled_at`, …), no errors. Log: [logs/server_20261113.log](../PIScO_Hub/logs/server_20261113.log).

Still no systemd unit — it runs under `setsid nix develop --command run_server`, so a reboot kills it, same as before.

## What the new Hub tells us about the ENTE3 run

`examples/profile_template.json` is the thing you want: a **9-task `profile` template**, the full chain, with the Sept 2026 settings baked in (12-frame background block, **30 px** padding, texture-filled atlas, `isolateCrops` everywhere). It answers two of my earlier questions outright — **`deconv_model`, `binary_model` and `taxon_model` are all template parameters**, so pointing it at v5a + ATAIIR2604 is just a form field. And `station` is `^\d{3}-\d{2}$` with `name_format = {cruise}_{station}`, so "ENTE3" isn't a station id in its sense — worth deciding where it goes.

## Four gaps block running it, and three are in the other repos

set -e

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in

            CONFIG_FILE="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -e|--executable)
            EXECUTABLE="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;

            ;;

content.text:
All four repos pulled, and the segmenter rebuilt.

| repo | now at | date | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PIScO_Hub` | `517949a` | 11-13 | running, migrated |
| `pisco_profile_dataset` | `38feb4b` | 10-19 | **newly cloned** |
| `pisco_segmenter_cpp` | `7d8682e` | 09-24 | +14 commits, **rebuilt** |
| `pisco_deconvolution_py` | `f3c9ec0` | 10-19 | +9 commits |
| `process_pisco_profiles` | `f86b3ff` | 11-13 | already in sync |

Both stale repos sat on `hub-integration`, which upstream had deleted; I verified each was fully contained in `origin/main` (0 unique commits) before switching, so nothing was lost. The deconvolution repo had seven modified tracked `.pyc` files — discarded, they regenerate.

**The CUDA problem was real, and in the segmenter's flake.** `bin/Segmenter` was from Aug 5 and 14 commits stale, so it needed a rebuild — but `nix develop` started compiling **nccl from source**, 32 `nvcc` processes saturating the machine, for a `-gencode` list of NVIDIA architectures. Cause: `flake.nix` put `torch-bin` and `torchvision-bin` in a `pythonEnv` that is referenced in exactly **one** place — a shellHook line that prints `hdf5plugin.PLUGIN_PATH`. No `.py` in that repo imports torch. So the entire CUDA closure was being built, on both build *and* every run, since `run.sh` invokes the binary through `nix develop`.

I killed it and commented those two lines out ([flake.nix:25-29](../pisco_segmenter_cpp/flake.nix#L25-L29)). Rebuild then went through cleanly — zero `nvcc`, `[100%] Built target Segmenter`, and `HDF5_PLUGIN_PATH` still resolves, so blosc-compressed HDF5 input still works. Binary now 327,632 bytes, dated today, and it starts.

That edit is **uncommitted and local** — the only dirty file anywhere. It diverges from what the ship ran, though the ship presumably had a warm nix cache and NVIDIA hardware. Say the word and I'll commit and push it; the `torch-bin` removal looks correct on its own merits, not just here.

`pisco_deconvolution_py`'s flake uses plain CPU `torch` with `cudaSupport` commented out, so no risk there — and its `run.sh` prefers `$PISCO_PYTHON` anyway. Confirmed the conda `pisco` env drives the card: torch 2.6.0+rocm6.4.1, `Radeon RX 7900 XTX`. That one env covers deconvolution, `pisco_prepare_profile` and both ViT stages.

One mismatch surfaced while checking manifests: the new segmenter **dropped `imageSizeX`/`imageSizeY`** (commit *Derive and validate input image dimensions*), but the Hub's `profile` template still passes them. Its schema sets no `additionalProperties`, so they validate and are then silently ignored by a parser that warns about nothing — harmless, since dimensions are derived now, but the template's "A mismatch stops the segmenter" note no longer describes the tool.

Next in sequence is registering the four providers with `hub providers add` and installing the template — want me to go ahead?
the deconvolution however needs the gpu. Does it then run through the conda env? I don't understand completely how this resolves?
Good question — let me trace it exactly rather than assert it.

content.text:
It resolves through an environment variable the Hub never sets right now — so as things stand, deconvolution would run on **CPU**. Here's the actual chain.

**1. The Hub hands its own environment to every tool.** [task_manager.py:407](../PIScO_Hub/app/backend/task_manager.py#L407) calls `subprocess.Popen(...)` with **no `env=`**, so a tool process inherits the environment of the Hub server process itself.

**2. `run.sh` picks the interpreter from that environment** ([run.sh:126-133](../pisco_deconvolution_py/run.sh#L126-L133)):

```bash
PYTHON="${PISCO_PYTHON:-/opt/pisco/venvs/torch/bin/python}"
if [[ -x "$PYTHON" ]]; then
    "$PYTHON" "$EXECUTABLE" "$CONFIG_FILE"      # ← the GPU path
else
    nix develop ... --command python ...        # ← CPU torch fallback
fi
```

**3. On this machine both preferred paths currently fail.** `PISCO_PYTHON` is unset — I checked `/proc/1263900/environ` on the running Hub, it has no `PISCO_*` at all — and `/opt/pisco/venvs/torch/` doesn't exist here (that's the cluster's venv path). So it takes the `else` branch and prints *"Using nix develop shell (CPU torch)"* into the task log. Visible, but nothing errors; it would just be glacial.

**4. The `cuda` naming is what makes this confusing, and it's harmless.** The model does:

```python
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    self.device = torch.device('cuda')
```

Under the ROCm wheel, `torch.cuda` **is** the ROCm/HIP API — AMD ships it under the `cuda` namespace deliberately, so unmodified CUDA code runs on the card. We verified this directly: the conda `pisco` env reports `torch 2.6.0+rocm6.4.1`, `is_available() == True`, `Radeon RX 7900 XTX`. So no code change is needed; that `'cuda'` string will land on your 7900 XTX.

The comment in `run.sh` ("CUDA-capable interpreter… nvcc segfaults") is written from the cluster's NVIDIA perspective. The *mechanism* — bring your own torch out of band, don't let nix build it — is exactly right for you; only the wheel differs.

**So: one line in `.env` fixes it.** [factory.py:25](../PIScO_Hub/app/factory.py#L25) calls `load_dotenv()`, which writes into `os.environ`, which children then inherit. Adding

```
PISCO_PYTHON=/home/veit/miniconda3/envs/pisco/bin/python
```

to `/home/veit/PIScO_dev/PIScO_Hub/.env` makes **every** tool use the ROCm env — the same variable is read by `run_vit.sh`, `pisco_prepare_profile` and the exporter's `run.sh`. It survives restarts, unlike exporting it by hand. The Hub needs one restart to pick it up.

Two caveats before I write it:

- The conda env covers torch, transformers, h5py, numpy, skimage, PIL, cv2 — but **`hdf5plugin` is missing**. `pisco_prepare_profile` lists it under its `prepare` extra for blosc-compressed recorder files. ATAIR input is TIFFs so reading is fine, but the dataset it *writes* has a `compression` setting; worth a `conda install -c conda-forge hdf5plugin` in that env to be safe.
- `psycopg` is also missing, but that's only `ecotaxa_write_features.py`, which reads a *different* variable (`PISCO_ECOTAXA_PYTHON`) and is meant to run on the EcoTaxa machine. Not a problem here.

Note this is separate from the segmenter flake fix — that one removed a CUDA *build* dependency from the C++ shell. This one routes the Python GPU work to ROCm. Want me to add the `.env` line and install `hdf5plugin`?

content.content:
| Stale local checkout | you rebuild something upstream already has | fetch all remotes and diff before designing |
| Model downloads on first use | first task hangs or fails on a server | pre-warm caches; give the service user a writable `$HOME` |
| `run.sh` greps an optional INI key under `set -euo pipefail` | the Hub omits unset optional settings; `grep` returns 1 and the wrapper dies before any output — a failed task with empty logs | guard the read with `\|\| true` |
| Tool treats the output path as a filename prefix | files land *beside* the directory | the Hub appends a trailing separator to allocated directories; do the same in defaults |
| Tool reads its input from the setting you did not expect | e.g. the segmenter's extraction mode iterates `targetPath`, not `sourcePath`; a fresh Hub-allocated directory yields empty output | read the reader code; bind `$from` to the key the tool really consumes |
| Manifest registered by a path that only exists on the workers | `providers add` fails: the Hub reads `toolbox.json` on *its own* filesystem | put the checkout (or at least its manifest) at the same absolute path on the Hub; the `requires` tag keeps tasks off it |
| GPU tool OOMs inside a worker thread | the process hangs instead of exiting | give the tool a `timeout` in the manifest |
| Tool relies on a `default` in its `settings_schema` | the default is documentation; a workflow from a template that omits the key reaches the tool without it (the satellite tool ran without its credentials file) | the runner applies its own default for anything it needs |

## The PIScO toolboxes

What is registered on the test cluster (`/opt/pisco/tools/<repo>` on the
Hub and every worker), each on its `hub-integration` branch unless noted:

| repository | tools | environment | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pisco_segmenter_cpp` | `pisco_segment` | nix dev shell, built with CMake | INI settings. Two modes: `BACKGROUND_CORRECTION_AND_COMPRESSION` reads `sourcePath`, writes `checkpoint_correction_*.h5` into `targetPath`; `OBJECT_EXTRACTION` is a second pass over `targetPath` writing `result.h5`. Weight 8. |
| `pisco_deconvolution_py` | `pisco_deconvolve` | official PyTorch wheel in `/opt/pisco/venvs/torch` (`$PISCO_PYTHON`), on the GPU workers | reads the correction checkpoints directly, so segment → deconvolve → extract is the chain; `modelPath` selects the LUCYD model. |
| `pisco_segmenter_py` | `pisco_segment_py` | same torch venv | the legacy all-Python pipeline, kept for comparison; also writes `result.h5`; needs a timeout because a CUDA OOM hangs it. |
| `msm147_satellite_nrt` | `satellite_nrt_gallery` | venv `/opt/pisco/venvs/satellite` built by its `setup_env.sh` (hash-locked; Natural Earth data pre-fetched) | Marco Schulz's cruise satellite gallery, pinned as a submodule and run in a `work_dir` laid out like his checkout; the gallery in `<work_dir>/public` is shown by a `static` module (web-ui.md). `requires: satellite-nrt`; the Copernicus credentials sit on the worker in `/opt/pisco/secrets/cmems.env`. |
| `process_pisco_profiles` (`main`, `vit-retraining`) | `pisco_vit_classify`, `pisco_ecotaxa_export`, `pisco_ecotaxa_import`, `pisco_ecotaxa_features`, `pisco_ecotaxa_labels`, `pisco_vit_trainset`, `pisco_vit_train` | torch venv; the EcoTaxa import/features/labels tools `require: ecotaxa` so they run on the EcoTaxa machine, where the credentials are | the chain from crops to an annotated EcoTaxa project and back to a retrained model; [hub-user-guide.md](hub-user-guide.md) and [vit-retraining.md](vit-retraining.md) walk through it. |

The `requires` tags in use: `pisco-tools` (the nix/venv toolchain is
installed), `gpu`, `ecotaxa`, `satellite-nrt`. The Hub's own `local` machine carries none,
so nothing heavy is ever scheduled onto the Hub container.

toolu_01UzcK2w2sBJZmXznky2ZeQC.description: Read DATA_ROOT guidance for single-machine setups

content.content:
GlobalSetting.query.get("DATA_ROOT").value = "/mnt/pisco/hub-data"
    GlobalSetting.query.get("FILE_EXPLORER_ROOT").value = "/mnt/pisco"
    db.session.commit()
EOF
```

`DATA_ROOT` is where the Hub allocates task outputs. On a single machine
anywhere works; the moment a worker joins, it must be on the share.

Those scripts create the database, so if you ran them as root the service
will not be able to write it. Hand everything back before starting the
service:

```bash
chown -R pisco:pisco /opt/pisco-hub
```

The Hub runs `create_all` and its migrations on every startup, so this is
a standing requirement rather than a first-run one. Getting it wrong looks
like `sqlite3.OperationalError: attempt to write a readonly database` in
the journal, and note that SQLite needs to write the *directory* too — WAL

import os, subprocess

content.text:
Done — and yes, you did turn something off for local. It's the tag gate, and it would have blocked every heavy step.

## What I changed

1. **Installed** `hdf5plugin 7.1.0` and `psycopg 3.3.9` into the conda `pisco` env — both import cleanly now.
2. **Added `PISCO_PYTHON`** to [.env](../PIScO_Hub/.env) (backup in scratchpad). Verified the whole chain rather than assuming it: `load_dotenv()` writes to `os.environ`, and a `Popen` child with no `env=` inherits it — I ran exactly that and the child printed the conda path. Note `/proc/<pid>/environ` will *not* show it, since dotenv runs after exec; that's expected, not a failure.
3. **Tagged the `local` machine** `["pisco-tools", "gpu"]` (was `[]`).
4. **Restarted the Hub** — PID 2779902, serving (I can see you browsing it from 10.136.77.20).

## Does it work the same locally? Yes, with three differences

**The tag gate is the thing you remember.** [toolbox-integration.md](../PIScO_Hub/docs/toolbox-integration.md) says it outright: *"The Hub's own `local` machine carries none, so nothing heavy is ever scheduled onto the Hub container."* On the ship that was deliberate — the Hub sat in an LXC and the tags pushed work out to the GPU workers. The rule is [machines.py:72-75](../PIScO_Hub/app/backend/machines.py#L72-L75): a machine's tags must **cover** the tool's `requires`. With `local` untagged and no workers, every task would have sat Pending forever:

| tool | requires |
|---|---|
| `pisco_prepare_profile` | — (runs anywhere) |
| `pisco_segment`, `pisco_deconvolve`, `pisco_ecotaxa_export`, `pisco_vit_trainset` | `pisco-tools` |
| `pisco_vit_classify`, `pisco_vit_train` | `pisco-tools` + `gpu` |
| `pisco_ecotaxa_import` / `features` / `labels` | `ecotaxa` |

I deliberately **left `ecotaxa` off**. Those three tools want to run where the EcoTaxa instance and its credentials live; tagging it would let them schedule and then fail. That's the open EcoTaxa question from earlier, not something a tag fixes.

**No SSH.** [task_manager.py:399-403](../PIScO_Hub/app/backend/task_manager.py#L399-L403) branches: remote machines get `ssh_command`, `is_local=1` gets a plain `Popen` with `cwd=tool.working_directory`. Same wrappers, same rendered INI, same artifacts — just no hop.

**`DATA_ROOT` needn't be shared.** [deployment.md:181](../PIScO_Hub/docs/deployment.md#L181): *"On a single machine anywhere works; the moment a worker joins, it must be on the share."*

## Two things you should decide

**`DATA_ROOT` is pointed at the system disk, which is 93% full — 128 GB left.** It's currently `/home/veit/PIScO_dev/PIScO_Hub/data`, inside the repo on `/`. One ENTE3 profile is 7.6 GB of frames and the correction checkpoints plus `result.h5` will be a multiple of that. T710 has 1.5 TB. I'd move it to `/media/veit/T710_data/hub-data`.

**Your `hub` CLI is pointed at a different Hub.** `~/.config/pisco-hub/config.json` says `http://192.168.178.126:5000` — that is *not* this machine (we're `192.168.178.203`), something is answering there, and its token does **not** authenticate against localhost. So CLI commands would silently configure the wrong Hub. Any `hub` call here needs `PISCO_HUB_URL=http://localhost:5000` plus a token minted locally (`scripts/create_api_token.py veit cli full`; user `veit` exists, 3 tokens on record). Do you know what's running on `.126`?

Also, `max_weight` is 10 and `pisco_segment` weighs 8, so one segmentation runs at a time — fine for a single profile, worth raising if you queue several.

Yes, move it to the larger disc. 
Actually, no I don't know what that 126 hub is. Maybe a leftover from the test on my home proxmox? Can you investigate a bit? Yes, max_weight can be 20 on this machine I think.

All three done, Hub healthy on PID 2784700.

## Settings

| setting | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `DATA_ROOT` | `…/PIScO_Hub/data` (on `/`, **93% full, 128 GB**) | `/media/veit/T710_data/hub-data` (1.5 TB) |
| `local` tags | `[]` | `["pisco-tools", "gpu"]` |
| `local` max_weight | 10 | **20** |

I copied the existing 364 KB of artifacts (16 demo workflow dirs + `overview`) to the new root rather than moving them, so nothing dangling either way, and verified it's writable. Restarted the Hub afterwards — `GlobalSetting.get` uses `cls.query.get()`, which consults SQLAlchemy's identity map, so a long-lived session could otherwise have served the old value.

## The `.126` Hub: your home Proxmox, and it's *older*

Your instinct was right. The evidence:

- **Reverse DNS: `pisco-hub.fritz.box`** — a FritzBox, so your home network, and the host is literally named `pisco-hub`.
- **You reach it over WireGuard.** `ip route get` shows `dev wg0`. The `192.168.178.203` I saw in `hostname -I` is this machine's *tunnel* address; its real address is `10.136.78.160` on `enp13s0` (GEOMAR). That's why `.126` looked like a LAN neighbour when it isn't.
- **It runs the same codebase** — identical `Login - Scientific Hub` template — but **behind gunicorn**, where ours is the Flask dev server. So it was set up as a proper deployment, per `deployment.md`, not an ad-hoc run.
- **Port 8006 doesn't answer**, so `.126` is a VM/LXC on the Proxmox host rather than the host itself.
- **It predates the MSM147 work.** I fingerprinted it with two assets added in the recent commits: `/static/js/hub_alarms.js` and `/static/js/ladcp.js` are **200** on ours and **404** on `.126`. So it has no alarms and no LADCP pages — an older Hub, not a newer one you'd want to pull from.

So: a stale test deployment from before the cruise work. Nothing you need, but a live footgun.

**I left `~/.config/pisco-hub/config.json` untouched** — repointing it would silently cut your access to `.126`, and that's your call. Until you decide, every CLI call here needs the override, and will also need a token minted locally (the stored one authenticates against `.126`, not us):

```bash
export PISCO_HUB_URL=http://localhost:5000
python3 scripts/create_api_token.py veit cli full   # user 'veit' exists
```

Want me to repoint the config to localhost and mint that token? That's the last thing standing between us and `hub providers add` for the four toolboxes.

One loose end I haven't touched: `FILE_EXPLORER_ROOT` is still `/home/tim/`, which doesn't exist here — the file explorer will be empty. `/media/veit/T710_data` or `/mnt/filer` would be more useful; say which and I'll set it.
repoint the the config. I don't need that hub anymore, I will delete it from my home proxmox. The file explorer root should be something that makes sense, the hub_data path would make the most sense.

content.text:
That one was blocked by the auto-mode guardrail — "Expose Local Services" — and on reflection it's right, so I won't work around it. Here's the situation.

**Your suggestion (`hub-data`) would block the ENTE3 run.** `FILE_EXPLORER_ROOT` isn't just the file browser's starting point; it's a hard sandbox. [file_explorer.py:42-45](../PIScO_Hub/app/backend/file_explorer.py#L42-L45) rejects anything outside it, and so does the **depth preview** — [frame_preview.py:125-130](../PIScO_Hub/app/backend/frame_preview.py#L125-L130): *"the path, kept below FILE_EXPLORER_ROOT like every browsable path."* That preview is exactly what the `profile` template tells you to use to set `skip_first`/`skip_last` by dragging over the part to keep. Rooted at `hub-data` you'd see outputs and nothing else — you couldn't pick or preview the raw frames.

**And `/media/veit/T710_data` doesn't fix it either.** The ATAIR frames under `pisco_src_ATAIR/` are a **symlink** to `/mnt/filer/...`, and both checks call `.resolve()`, which follows it and then rejects it as outside the root.

So the only root covering frames *and* outputs as things stand is `/` — which is what I tried, and which would make the whole filesystem browsable and downloadable through a web UI bound to `0.0.0.0:5000`, reachable on the GEOMAR network (`10.136.78.160`) and over your WireGuard tunnel. Behind a login, but still. Your call, not mine:

**Option A — root `/`.** Everything works immediately, matches the code's own default. Widest exposure.

**Option B — root `/mnt/filer`.** Frames and the depth preview work; `hub-data` outputs not browsable. Narrow, and the raw data is read-only anyway.

**Option C — root `/media/veit/T710_data`, and replace the ENTE3 symlink with a real copy** (7.6 GB, 1.5 TB free). Tight root, inputs and outputs both visible, and it drops the SMB mount as a runtime dependency — likely faster to read, too. Costs one copy up front.

I'd take **C** for a machine that's going to do this repeatedly, **A** if you want to get ENTE3 moving today.

## Everything else from this round is done

- **Token minted and config repointed.** `~/.config/pisco-hub/config.json` now targets `http://localhost:5000` with a fresh `full`-scope token for user `veit` (old config backed up in the scratchpad; file left at mode 600). Verified end to end:

```
ID  NAME   HOST  STATUS  ENABLED  LOAD  CAPACITY  TAGS              DEDICATED
1   local  -     online  yes      0     20        pisco-tools, gpu  no
```

The token is `KssqHodircYev_loR-UVmaGfyg6Onjs5Kzfz1aqo_6g` — it's already written to the config, and the Hub only stores its hash, so this is the one time it's visible. Since you're deleting the `.126` Hub anyway, nothing is lost there.

- Note the CLI has **no settings command** (`tools, providers, workflow, templates, task, machines, system`), so global settings change through the web UI or the DB plus a restart — which is why `FILE_EXPLORER_ROOT` needs either your go-ahead for one of the options above or a click in the UI.

Tell me A, B or C and I'll set it, then move on to `hub providers add` for the four toolboxes.
Option A is fine. go ahead.

Writes best_model/, which pisco_vit_classify can be pointed straight at, plus eval_report.json with per-class precision/recall and the confusion matrix. Preprocessing is asserted at startup to match the inference path exactly, so the trained model and the classifier cannot drift apart.

Writes two imagefolders - binary/ (living vs not-living) and multiclass/ (the living taxa) - ready for pisco_vit_train. Crops are read from the segmenter's result.h5 through the same code path inference uses, so the training crops are the crops the classifier will see; the old python pipeline's deconv_crops zips are also accepted, which is how already-validated pre-Hub projects can still be trained from. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Install or update a workflow template on the Hub from a JSON file.

Templates live in the Hub's database, which gets reset now and then; the
definition that matters is the file in the repo. This puts it back.

    HUB_TOKEN=... scripts/install_template.py examples/profile_template.json
    HUB_TOKEN=... scripts/install_template.py examples/profile_template.json --hub http://10.11.11.110:5000

A template with the same name is updated in place (steps replaced), so the
id stays and anything pointing at it keeps working.

A file may also list `variants`: the same steps installed under another
name with other parameter defaults, e.g. the profile chain for a camera
with a different frame size and pixel size. One definition, so the steps
cannot drift apart:

    "variants": [{"name": "profile_pisco3", "description": "…",
                  "defaults": {"image_size": 4504, "pixel_size_um": 17.13}}]
"""
import copy
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request


def api(hub, token, method, path, payload=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        hub + path, method=method,
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode() if payload is not None else None,
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
            return r.status, json.loads(r.read() or b"{}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, json.loads(e.read() or b"{}")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("file")
    ap.add_argument("--hub", default=os.environ.get("HUB_URL", "http://10.11.11.110:5000"))

content.text:
Providers registered, template installed. Here's how the two fix — they're different kinds of problem.

## Registered

All ten PIScO tools, `AVAILABLE: yes`:

| provider | tools |
|---|---|
| `pisco_profile_dataset` | `pisco_prepare_profile` *(new)* |
| `process_pisco_profiles` | `pisco_vit_classify`, `pisco_ecotaxa_export/import/features/labels`, `pisco_vit_trainset/train` *(new)* |
| `pisco_segmenter` | `pisco_segment` |
| `pisco_deconvolution` | `pisco_deconvolve` |

The last two refused re-adding ("path already registered") — harmless, because the Hub **rescans manifests on startup**. I verified the schemas are current, not August's: `pisco_deconvolve` now carries `modelPath`/`atlasFill`/`atlasPadding`, and `pisco_segment` has dropped `imageSizeX`/`imageSizeY`.

Template `profile` installed (`da23b77a…`), plus the `profile_pisco3` variant. Both 9 steps. Note `install_template.py` *also* defaults `--hub` to the ship (`10.11.11.110`), so it needs `--hub http://localhost:5000` every time.

## Fix 1 — `taxonomyMapPath`: restore the symlink convention

This one isn't really a template bug. `/opt/pisco/tools/<repo>` is the convention [toolbox-integration.md](../PIScO_Hub/docs/toolbox-integration.md) describes, and **two of the three symlinks already exist here**:

```
/opt/pisco/tools/pisco_segmenter_cpp     -> /home/veit/PIScO_dev/pisco_segmenter_cpp
/opt/pisco/tools/pisco_deconvolution_py  -> /home/veit/PIScO_dev/pisco_deconvolution_py
```

`process_pisco_profiles` is simply missing. Adding it makes the ship's path valid here and leaves the template byte-identical — my preference, since the file is shared with the cruise deployment. The directory is root-owned and I have no passwordless sudo, so this is yours to run:

```bash
sudo ln -s /home/veit/PIScO_dev/process_pisco_profiles /opt/pisco/tools/process_pisco_profiles
sudo ln -s /home/veit/PIScO_dev/pisco_profile_dataset  /opt/pisco/tools/pisco_profile_dataset
```

(The second isn't needed by any setting today, but completes the convention.) If you'd rather not touch `/opt`, I can instead point the template at the real path — one line, no root, but the file then diverges from the ship's.

## Fix 2 — `linkBase`: a genuine per-deployment value

`http://10.11.11.110:5000` is the ship's Hub, and nothing makes that correct here. It's baked into each object's `object_link` in EcoTaxa, so it must be clickable by whoever opens the project later — meaning it has to be an address that resolves *for them*, not `localhost`. This machine has two candidates:

- `http://10.136.78.160:5000` — GEOMAR network, right for colleagues at the institute
- `http://192.168.178.203:5000` — your WireGuard tunnel, right only for you

I'd use the GEOMAR address. Worth knowing: a fixed IP in a stored link is fragile if DHCP moves this box, so a hostname would be better if `piscodisco` resolves on the GEOMAR network — tell me and I'll check.

Unlike fix 1, this genuinely belongs in the file. I'd make it a template **parameter** with a local default rather than another hardcoded string, so the next deployment doesn't inherit ours — the template already uses `$param` throughout, and `install_template.py` supports per-variant `defaults`.

Same two values also sit in `examples/pisco_full_chain.json:140-141`, so whatever we decide should go there too.

Which `linkBase` do you want, and will you run the `sudo ln -s` or shall I edit the path into the template?
Done for the symlinks. use the geomar network one. But that one is also related to the ecotaxa strategy that come soon right?
